_doc: The illustrated chronicle (systems/chronicleBook.js, ui/chronicleBook.js): the Annals made into a book to export — a self-contained HTML file with the House's arms, a chapter per ruler with a portrait and a map of the realm at the reign's end, the key battles, great works and deaths, a dynasty tree and an appendix from Deeds & Records and the Ledger. The maps are border snapshots taken as the game runs (house.chronicleBook.maps): a coarse grid of realm cells, run-length encoded, at the founding, at each reign's end, when a crown is won or lost, and every `eraYears` years. `maxCols` bounds a map's width in cells, `mapCap` the maps kept (the era maps are thinned first), so a century of play saves a few tens of kilobytes. `moments` sorts the House chronicle (house.history) into the book's three lists by tag, else by a word in the line; `momentCap` lines a list keeps per reign (a closed reign's are filed when it ends, so they outlive the chronicle's cap).

battleLines._doc: How House.recordBattle tells a battle in the House chronicle (tagged war + battle, or siege, so the book's battles list has it with its date, place, foe and outcome). By kind (field, sea, assault, siege) and outcome; {who} the commander, {foe} the enemy, {place} the town, {at} 'at X' / 'near X' (a town within `near` steps) / 'in the hills'. A foe weaker than `minStrength` is a skirmish and not chronicled.

sea.defeat: {who} was defeated by {foe} in a sea battle {at}.

assault.defeat: {who}'s assault on {place} was thrown back by {foe}.

labels.founding: The realm at the founding of {house}
labels.end: The realm at the death of {name}
labels.crownWon: The realm as {name} took the crown of {crown}
labels.crownLost: The realm as the crown of {crown} passed from {house}
labels.final: The realm as this book was written, in the year {year}

_prose: Where the language model has written the book's prose (systems/llmProse.js, LlmProse.text(world, key, fallback)), the book prints it in place of the template text. `proseKeys` are the keys tried, in order, per part: {house} is the House's id, {chapter} the Annals chapter id (g<gen>_<startDay>). The foreword and the epilogue are asked of LlmProse.write when the book is exported (kind 'foreword' / 'epilogue'), and read from their templates until written.
foreword: Here are set down the deeds of {house}: {generations} {generationsWord} of rulers, from the year {from} to the year {to}. What the scribes saw, they wrote; what they did not, the maps remember.
forewordEnded: Here are set down the deeds of {house}, from the year {from} until the line ended in the year {to}: {generations} {generationsWord}, and what was won and lost between.
epilogue: So the book closes in the year {to}, with {last} at the head of {house}. The rest is yet to be written.
epilogueEnded: So ends the line of {house}, in the year {to}, with {last}. {rank}.
